# Chapter I - Preliminary {#c1}

## A. Short Title and Commencement {#a}

1. These Directions shall be called the Fixture Direction (Commercial Banks - Customer Due Diligence), 2025.

2. These Directions apply to every commercial bank, including branches and majority-owned subsidiaries located abroad, to the extent they are not contradictory to the local laws of the host country.

# Chapter II - Small Accounts {#c2}

## B. Small Accounts {#b}

3. A bank may open a small account for an individual who does not possess an officially valid document, subject to the following conditions:

(a) the aggregate of all credits in a financial year does not exceed rupees two lakh;

(b) the aggregate of all withdrawals and transfers in a month does not exceed rupees twenty thousand;

(c) the balance at any point of time does not exceed rupees one lakh.

4. A small account shall remain operational for an initial period of twelve months. The bank may extend it once by a further twelve months if the holder shows that an application for an officially valid document has been made.

# Chapter III - Risk Management {#c3}

## C. Periodic Updation {#c}

5. A bank shall carry out periodic updation of customer due diligence information at least once every two years for high risk customers, once every eight years for medium risk customers and once every ten years for low risk customers, from the date of opening of the account or the last updation.

6. Where a low risk individual customer confirms through a self-declaration that there is no change in KYC information, the bank shall accept the declaration through email, mobile number registered with the bank, digital channels or a letter, and shall not insist on a fresh set of documents.

## D. Beneficial Ownership {#d}

7. Where the customer is a company, the beneficial owner is the natural person who, whether acting alone or together, has a controlling ownership interest of more than ten percent of the shares or capital or profits of the company.

8. Where the customer is a partnership firm, the beneficial owner is the natural person who has ownership of or entitlement to more than ten percent of the capital or profits of the partnership.

# Chapter IV - Repeal and Saving {#c4}

## E. Repeal {#e}

9. With the issue of these Directions, the Fixture Direction - Customer Due Diligence, 2016 issued vide FIX.AML.BC.No.81/14.01.001/2015-16 dated February 25, 2016 stands repealed.
